en.title: Countable and uncountable nouns
en.summary: Countable nouns can be counted one by one; uncountable nouns cannot.

paragraphs: Countable nouns name things we can count one by one: one book, two books. Uncountable nouns name things we see as a mass or as a whole, such as water, rice, advice or music. The difference matters because it decides which small words we can use with the noun.

An uncountable noun has no plural form and takes a singular verb. It cannot take a or an. Use much and a little with uncountable nouns, and many and a few with countable nouns. To count an uncountable noun, use a unit: a glass of water, a piece of news.

Advice, information, news, furniture, luggage, homework and weather are uncountable in English, though their equivalents are countable in many languages. We say The news is good and I have some homework.

Some nouns have both uses with different meanings. Paper is a material, but a paper is a newspaper or an essay. Coffee is a drink, and a coffee is one cup of it. Time is uncountable, but three times means three occasions.

items: Wrong: **The news are good.** Right: **The news is good.**

ro.title: Substantive numărabile și nenumărabile
ro.summary: Substantivele numărabile pot fi numărate, iar substantivele nenumărabile denumesc de obicei materii sau noțiuni abstracte.

paragraphs: Substantivele numărabile numesc lucruri pe care le putem număra. Ele au forme de singular și de plural. Substantivele nenumărabile denumesc lichide, materiale sau idei abstracte. Pe acestea nu le numărăm bucată cu bucată.

Substantivele numărabile se pot folosi cu numerale sau cuvinte precum „mulți” și „puține”. Substantivele nenumărabile stau de obicei doar la singular. Pentru ele folosim cuvinte precum „mult”, „puțin” sau unități de măsură.
